body:
Source: GitHub issue #793 (release-audit class false-green, P1-high). Re-verified on main @ e0768ff9: `packages/tickets/bin/adlc-tickets.mjs`'s doctor branch (around line 139) is `emit(doctorTicketStore(store, { root, archive: Boolean(flags.archive), key }), flags.json); return;` — it prints the result object and returns WITHOUT ever setting `process.exitCode`, so a failing check (an unresolved recovery transaction, a broken/unsigned manifest chain, a stale/malformed active-ticket pointer) is printed as `"ok": false` while the process itself exits 0. This directly contradicts `docs/specs/sharded-ticket-store.md` §9 ('2: invalid contract, stale snapshot, conflict, unresolved recovery, or policy deny') and the SIBLING implementation in `packages/ticket-sync/lib/doctor.mjs`, which already gets this right: `return { exitCode: ok ? 0 : 2, ok, checks };`. Note `exitCodeFor` IS already imported into `adlc-tickets.mjs` (line 15) and IS already used elsewhere in the same file — at `main().catch(...)`'s error handler (around line 245-247: `process.exitCode = exitCodeFor(structured);`) — just not on the doctor branch's SUCCESSFUL (non-throwing) return path, which is exactly where this bug lives: `doctorTicketStore` returning `{ ok: false, ... }` is not an exception, so the catch handler never sees it.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package `packages/tickets`: bin/adlc-tickets.mjs (the CLI dispatcher — many `command === '...'` branches; the doctor branch is one of them), lib/doctor.mjs (`doctorTicketStore(store, opts)` — returns the `{ok, checks, ...}` result object; do not change its return shape), lib/errors.mjs (`exitCodeFor(error)` — currently takes a `TicketStoreError`-shaped object; check its exact signature/logic before deciding whether to reuse it directly on the doctor result or write a small parallel mapping — the doctor result may not be a `TicketStoreError` instance, so `exitCodeFor` might not apply as-is; if not, a minimal `ok ? 0 : 2` is exactly what ticket-sync's sibling does and is sufficient — do not overengineer a generalized error-classification scheme for this one call site). Tests: `npm test -w packages/tickets` (large suite; scope your new test narrowly and do not need to touch unrelated files). `test/doctor.test.mjs` already exists — read it first to see what's already covered (the RESULT OBJECT'S shape) versus what's missing (the PROCESS EXIT CODE, which a test invoking the CLI as a real bin process must check, not just calling `doctorTicketStore` directly as a library function).

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. On the doctor branch in `adlc-tickets.mjs`, after computing the result, set `process.exitCode = result.ok ? 0 : 2` (or route through `exitCodeFor`/an equivalent existing helper IF it genuinely applies to this result shape without distorting other exit codes — verify this by reading `exitCodeFor`'s body first; if it does not cleanly apply, the direct `ok ? 0 : 2` ternary, matching ticket-sync's own doctor exactly, is the correct minimal fix) BEFORE calling `emit(...)`, or immediately after — order relative to `emit` does not matter as long as `process.exitCode` is set on every doctor invocation, success or failure.
2. `emit(...)`'s printed output is UNCHANGED — this is an exit-code fix only, not an output-format change.
3. Every OTHER command branch in this file is UNCHANGED — do not touch `list`, `export`, or any other branch's exit-code handling; this ticket is scoped to the doctor branch alone.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 A store with a pending unresolved recovery transaction (`.adlc/ticket-transactions/<uuid>/journal.json` present, per the issue's own repro): `adlc ticket doctor --json` prints `ok: false` in its JSON AND the process exits with status 2 (spawn the real bin, assert `process.exitCode`/child exit status, not just the printed object). verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/doctor-exit-code.test.mjs`
- AC2 A healthy store: `adlc ticket doctor --json` prints `ok: true` and exits 0 (regression). verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/doctor-exit-code.test.mjs`
- AC3 A store with a broken/unsigned manifest chain (or any other individual `ok:false` check the existing `doctorTicketStore` already detects — reuse an existing fixture pattern from `test/doctor.test.mjs` rather than inventing a new corruption mechanism) also exits 2. verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/doctor-exit-code.test.mjs`
- AC4 Non-JSON (text) mode doctor output also sets the same exit code — the fix is not `--json`-conditional. verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/doctor-exit-code.test.mjs`
- AC5 Existing suite green (confirm actual baseline count; if any existing test in `test/doctor.test.mjs` asserted a real bin-process exit of 0 on an `ok:false` doctor result, rewrite it and say so in the PR body — that would have been pinning the bug). verify: `npm test -w packages/tickets`
- AC6 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)

OUT OF SCOPE: any change to `doctorTicketStore`'s own detection logic, its return shape, or any other CLI command's exit-code behaviour.

PROCESS (ADLC). Work only in your assigned worktree. P3: the rails on this ticket are frozen — if the fix appears to require editing a rail path, STOP and report; never set ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS. P4: TDD — write test/doctor-exit-code.test.mjs first, run it RED, then implement. P5 before opening the PR: the package suite, `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` (exit 0), then the cross-model review loop (see lane instructions) until a round is clean. Do not add gate-manifest entries. Keep the diff to packages/tickets/bin/adlc-tickets.mjs, the new test, and this ticket's shard. PR title `fix(tickets): ...`, body must contain `Closes #793`.
title: tickets: `adlc ticket doctor` sets a real exit code on ok:false, matching the spec and ticket-sync's sibling implementation
